title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Rab, Croatia 2027: Prices & Guide
metaDescription: Yes, Rab has all-inclusive: Arba Resort near Rab Town. See what is included, rough prices vs half-board and apartments, and who it suits.
content:
## Does Rab Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes, but the offer is small. Rab is mostly a island of private apartments, small family hotels and campsites. The one clear all-inclusive resort is **Arba Resort, Valamar Collection**, on the forested Capo Fronte peninsula near Kampor, about 5 km from Rab Town. It opened in 2025 and is positioned as a premium family resort. A second option is **San Marino Resort in Lopar**, a 3-star complex 14 km from Rab Town with access to the 1.5 km sandy Paradise Beach. Some booking sellers list it as all-inclusive. Availability of the board type changes by season and operator, so confirm it before paying.

Most other hotels on Rab, including the Valamar hotels around Rab Town and Lopar, sell breakfast or half-board. Do not assume an all-inclusive rate unless the booking page names it.

## What Is Included in All-Inclusive on Rab

At Arba Resort the package covers:

- Buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner in the main restaurant, plus a premium V Level restaurant for suite guests
- Soft drinks from the dispenser during meals, with wine and beer at lunch and dinner
- Snacks at set times
- Children's menu options, including baby-food choices
- Free sun loungers on the sandy beach below the resort for hotel guests
- Use of the outdoor pools and the entertainment programme

The resort has six indoor and outdoor pools and an 800 m² spa. Spa treatments are not included. Drinks outside meal times, premium spirits and restaurant visits in Rab Town are usually extra. Check the exact hours of the drinks and snack offer when booking, because they differ between hotels.

## Rough Prices Per Person Per Night

Resort rates are quoted per room and shift with date, room type and child discounts. The figures below are approximate planning numbers for two adults sharing a room.

| Board type | Shoulder season (May–June, September) | Peak season (mid-July–mid-August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive, Arba Resort | approx. €110–140 | approx. €170–230 |
| All-inclusive, Lopar 3-star | approx. €70–90 | approx. €100–120 |
| Half-board, small Lopar hotel | €34–46 | €56–65 |
| Private apartment, room only | approx. €20–30 | approx. €30–45 |

The half-board figures come from a real Lopar hotel price grid, where the cost climbs from €34 in the low season to €65 per person at the July–August peak. Apartment prices depend heavily on size. A two-bedroom unit split between four people can fall below €25 each, even in August. Luxury apartments and villas are a separate category; a deluxe apartment in Lopar can reach €330 per night in mid-summer.

## All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Private Apartment

Half-board costs about a third to a half of an upmarket all-inclusive rate. It makes sense when the days are spent at beaches and the evening meal is eaten at the hotel. An apartment is cheapest by far. A family of four spending €40–60 a day on groceries and one restaurant meal still pays much less than the resort. A coffee in Rab Town costs about €2–3 and a konoba main course €14–25, so eating out for every meal does add up.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits on Rab

**Families with small children.** This is the best fit. Meals at fixed times, children's menus, shallow sandy beach access and pools in one place remove daily planning. A short stay of 3–5 nights works well because the price premium covers convenience, not volume of use.

**Short breaks with no car.** Resort guests do not need to find a restaurant or a parking space. Rab Town is 5 km away and reachable by bike, local transport or taxi.

**Groups wanting entertainment.** Programmes for children and adults are built into the stay.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

- Stays of 7 nights or longer, where the premium adds up to several hundred euros
- Couples and adults without children, who gain little from kids' clubs
- Travellers who want to try Rab Town's restaurants, the old-town bars and the Lopar beaches
- Groups of 4–6 sharing one apartment

The all-inclusive idea sounds ideal for a family week, but on Rab it often wastes money. The island's strength is its beaches and small konobas, and a guest tied to the resort buffet at lunch and dinner skips both. Choose half-board or an apartment unless the children are under about 8.

## Insider Tips

- Book Arba Resort for shoulder season. June and September give the same pools and sea with much lower rates.
- Check ferry timing before arrival. The Stinica–Mišnjak ferry serves the south of Rab and the Valbiska–Lopar ferry the north. Arba lies in the south-west, so the Stinica route is usually the shorter drive from Zadar, while Rijeka airport is about 2 hours 40 minutes away including the Lopar crossing.
- Ask whether tourist tax is included. It is typically charged separately.
- If a resort rate looks cheap in Lopar, confirm the board type and the drinks hours in writing.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Alternatives

On Rab itself, Arba Resort is the main choice and San Marino Resort in Lopar the second to check. Outside Rab, the closest all-inclusive Valamar resorts are in Rabac, Istria, including Valamar Bellevue Resort and Girandella Family Hotel. They are reached by a ferry and a drive of around 2–3 hours, so treat them as a separate trip.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel on Rab?
faq.answer: Yes. Arba Resort, Valamar Collection, on Capo Fronte near Kampor, 5 km from Rab Town, sells all-inclusive. San Marino Resort in Lopar is also offered with all-inclusive by some sellers, so check the board type before booking.

faq.question: What does all-inclusive include on Rab?
faq.answer: Typically buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner, soft drinks, and wine or beer with lunch and dinner, plus snacks at set times. Spa treatments, drinks outside the set hours and outside restaurants are usually extra.

faq.question: How much is all-inclusive per person per night on Rab?
faq.answer: Roughly €110–140 at Arba Resort in shoulder season and €170–230 in peak summer, based on two adults sharing. A 3-star resort in Lopar costs about €70–120. Rates vary by room type and child discounts.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than a private apartment on Rab?
faq.answer: No. An apartment costs about €20–45 per person per night, and half-board in a small Lopar hotel costs €34–65. All-inclusive pays off only for families who use the pools, kids' programme and meals every day.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive good for families with small children on Rab?
faq.answer: Yes, particularly for stays of 3–7 nights. Fixed meals, children's menus, pools and a sandy beach below Arba Resort simplify the days. Longer stays are cheaper in an apartment.

quickAnswer: Yes, Rab has real all-inclusive. Arba Resort, Valamar Collection, on the Capo Fronte peninsula 5 km from Rab Town, sells it, with buffet meals, drinks with lunch and dinner, and snacks. Expect roughly €110–230 per person per night, about two to three times the cost of a self-catered apartment.
